arxiv-2107-01514.title: Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis with Observable Neutron-Anti-Neutron Oscillation
arxiv-2107-01514.creator: Rabindra N. Mohapatra a, Nobuchika Okada b
arxiv-2107-01514.description: Abstract We discuss the implications of Affleck-Dine (AD) baryogenesis for different classes of baryon and lepton number violating processes: specially focussing on implications for neutron-anti-neutron ( n − n ¯ n-\bar{n} ) oscillation. The class of AD baryogenesis scenarios we work with uses the AD field also as the inflaton which is nonminimally coupled to gravity.

arxiv-2209-09564.title: Stabilizer Approximation
arxiv-2209-09564.creator: Xinying Li, Jianan Wang, Chuixiong Wu, Fen Zuo
arxiv-2209-09564.description: Abstract We propose a heuristic method to obtain the approximate groundstate for a Hamiltonian in the qubit form, based on the stabilizer formalism. These states may serve as proper initial states for further refined computation. It would be interesting to assess the efficiency and scalability of the method.

arxiv-2310-16422.title: Topological Complexity Related To Multi-Valued Functions
arxiv-2310-16422.creator: MELİH İS
arxiv-2310-16422.description: Abstract . In this paper, we deal with the robot motion planning problem in multi-valued function theory. We first enrich the multi-homotopy studies by introducing a multi-homotopy lifting property and a multi-fibration. Then we compute both a topological multi-complexity and a Lusternik-Schnirelmann multi-category of a space or a multi-fibration. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 32A12, 55M30, 14D06, 14F35 1.

arxiv-2410-13321.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models via Summary-Guided Decoding
arxiv-2410-13321.creator: Kyungmin Min, Minbeom Kim, Kang-il Lee, Dongryeol Lee, Kyomin Jung
arxiv-2410-13321.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kyungmin Min, Minbeom Kim, Kang-il Lee, Dongryeol Lee, Kyomin Jung. Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities in generating detailed and coherent responses from visual inputs. However, they are prone to generate hallucinations due to an over-reliance on language priors. To address this issue, we investigate the language priors in LVLMs and make two key observations: (1) Even when predicting the tokens associated with image-related part-of-speech (POS), models increasingly rely on linguistic priors as the token sequences grow, thereby amplifying hallucinations.

arxiv-2504-07090.title: A Differentiable, End-to-End Forward Model for 21 cm Cosmology: Estimating the Foreground, Instrument, and Signal Joint Posterior
arxiv-2504-07090.creator: Nicholas Kern
arxiv-2504-07090.description: Abstract We present a differentiable, end-to-end Bayesian forward modeling framework for line intensity mapping cosmology experiments, with a specific focus on low-frequency radio telescopes targeting the redshifted 21 cm line from neutral hydrogen as a cosmological probe. Our framework is capable of posterior density estimation of the cosmological signal jointly with foreground and telescope parameters at the field level.

arxiv-2504-15808.title: Quantum Speed Limits in Qubit Dynamics Driven by Bistable Random Telegraph Noise: From Markovian to Non-Markovian Regimes
arxiv-2504-15808.creator: Maryam Hadipour
arxiv-2504-15808.description: Abstract We investigate the quantum speed limit (QSL) of a single superconducting qubit subjected to pure dephasing induced by bistable random telegraph noise (RTN), a common environmental disturbance in solid-state quantum systems. Using an exactly solvable model, we explore how the interplay between RTN parameters—the switching rate, coupling strength, and initial condition governs the transition between Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.

arxiv-2602-24096.title: DiffusionHarmonizer: Bridging Neural Reconstruction and Photorealistic Simulation with Online Diffusion Enhancer
arxiv-2602-24096.creator: Yuxuan Zhang, Katarína Tóthová, Zian Wang, Kangxue Yin, Haithem Turki, Riccardo de Lutio, Yen-Yu Chang, Or Litany, Sanja Fidler, Zan Gojcic, [-4mm] NVIDIA University of Toronto Cornell University Technion {alezhang, ktothova, zgojcic}@nvidia.com
arxiv-2602-24096.description: Abstract Simulation is essential to the development and evaluation of autonomous robots such as self-driving vehicles. Neural reconstruction is emerging as a promising solution as it enables simulating a wide variety of scenarios from real-world data alone in an automated and scalable way.

pmc-10696190.title: Hypoxia and inflammatory factor preconditioning enhances the immunosuppressive properties of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells
pmc-10696190.creator: Hang Li, Xiao-Qing Ji, Shu-Ming Zhang, Ri-Hui Bi
pmc-10696190.description: BACKGROUNDMesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have great potential for the treatment of various immune diseases due to their unique immunomodulatory properties. However, MSCs exposed to the harsh inflammatory environment of damaged tissue after intravenous transplantation cannot exert their biological effects, and therefore, their therapeutic efficacy is reduced.

pmc-10915921.title: Clinical Manifestations Laboratory Tests Abdominal Ultrasonic Findings and In-hospital Prognosis of COVID-19 in 185 Pediatric Cases in a Tertiary Center
pmc-10915921.creator: Maryam Jafari, Yasaman Mahalati, Elham Zarei, Mohammad Mahdi Kazemi, Arsalan Irompour, Amirhoessein Sadri, Hamed AzadiYekta
pmc-10915921.description: Background: Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, there is little information about the different clinical aspects of COVID-19 in children. In this study, we assessed the clinical manifestations, outcome, ultrasound, and laboratory findings of pediatric COVID-19. Methods: This retrospective study was conducted on 185 children with definitive diagnosis of COVID-19 between 2021 and 2022. The patients’ information was retrieved from hospital records.

pmc-11492580.title: Characterization of drusen formation in a primary porcine tissue culture model of dry AMD
pmc-11492580.creator: Erika M. Shaw, Alexander J. Tate, Ramesh Periasamy, Daniel M. Lipinski
pmc-11492580.description: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) affects millions of individuals worldwide and is a leading cause of blindness in the elderly. In dry AMD, lipoproteinaceous deposits called drusen accumulate between the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and Bruch’s membrane, leading to impairment of oxygen and nutrient trafficking to the neural retina, and degeneration of the overlying photoreceptor cells.

pmc-12443952.title: Impact of primary, specialist, and hospital care data on disease frequency estimates in older adults in Sweden
pmc-12443952.creator: Katharina Schmidt-Mende, Maria Feychting, Eric Chen, Javier Louro, Karin Modig
pmc-12443952.description: Nordic countries have a long-standing tradition of using administrative healthcare data from specialist and hospital settings to study disease frequency and etiological associations. While similar data are increasingly available elsewhere, large-scale primary care data remain limited. Understanding how data source affects disease identification is therefore critical.

pmc-13106355.title: Measuring daily time experience: development and validation of the Seven-Dimensional Time Quality of Life Scale
pmc-13106355.creator: Bowen Xue, Yuetan Liu, Xiaoying Jiang, Zhe Ni, Xiaohua Sun, Hong Luo
pmc-13106355.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMental health assessment has traditionally relied on symptom-based measures of depression and anxiety. Although widely used, such measures may overlook individuals’ everyday experiences and lifestyle contexts that are closely related to psychological well-being. Grounded in the Seven-Dimensional Time Theory (SDTT), the present study aimed to develop and validate the Seven-Dimensional Time Quality of Life Scale (SDT-QoLS) to assess the overall quality of daily time experience.MethodsUsing a convenience sampling approach, participants aged 12–65 years were recruited from a psychiatric outpatient setting.
